Capucine de Fouchier, an independent specialist in mental health and psychosocial support, focuses on planning and delivering occupational mental health services for humanitarian workers in the European region. Her expertise includes addressing inequality, social protection, and social determinants of health, particularly in the informal economy. 2. Samuel Harvey, a professor and executive director at the Black Dog Institute, University of New South Wales, Australia, specializes in occupational psychiatry, psychiatric epidemiology, and workplace mental health research in the Western Pacific region. 3. Hiroto Ito, a professor in the Department of Health Policy and Management at Tohoku Medical and Pharmaceutical University, Japan, focuses on health policy and management for occupational mental health and safety in the Western Pacific region. 4. Norito Kawakami, a professor in the Department of Mental Health at the Graduate School of Medicine, University of Tokyo, Japan, has expertise in occupational mental health, community mental health, and epidemiology in the Western Pacific region. 5. Spo Kgalamono, the executive director of the National Institute for Occupational Health in South Africa, works on occupational medicine and the implementation of occupational health services in lowand middle-income countries (LMICs) in the African region. 6. Nour Kik, a policy and advocacy coordinator for the National Mental Health Programme at the Ministry of Public Health in Lebanon, focuses on mental health policy and the implementation of national workplace mental health programs in the Eastern Mediterranean region. 7. Margaret Kitt, deputy director at the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), USA, and director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Occupational Health, specializes in occupational medicine and psychosocial risk policies in the Region of the Americas. 8. Anthony D. LaMontagne, a professor at the Institute for Health Transformation, Deakin University, Australia, focuses on applied epidemiology, workplace mental health, occupational health and safety interventions, and workplace policy interventions in the Western Pacific region. 9. Sapna Mahajan, director of Genomics and Society at Genome Canada, works on the development and implementation of workplace mental health standards at national, regional, and international levels, with a focus on public health in the Region of the Americas. 10. Seyed Kazem Malakouti, a professor at the Tehran Institute of Psychiatry, Iran University of Medical Sciences, and director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Mental Health, specializes in integrating mental health services into primary care, suicide prevention, and substance use prevention in the Eastern Mediterranean region. 11. Jose Luis Ayuso-Mateos, a professor in the Department of Psychiatry at the Autonomous University of Madrid, Spain, and director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Research and Training in Mental Health Services, focuses on epidemiology and interventions for mental disorders, chronic health conditions, and workplace inclusion in the European region. 12. Karina Nielsen, a professor at the Institute of Work Psychology, University of Sheffield, UK, specializes in the development, implementation, and evaluation of organizational interventions for mental well-being, organizational psychology, and return-to-work strategies in the European region. 13. Christopher Prinz, affiliated with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in France, focuses on employment and disability policy in the European region. 14. Pratap Sharan, a professor in the Department of Psychiatry at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, India, works on public mental health and the mental health of health workers in the South-East Asia region. 15. Katherine Sorsdahl, a professor in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Cape Town, South Africa, and co-director of the Alan J. Flisher Centre for Public Mental Health, focuses on global mental health and health systems strengthening in the African region. 16. Graham Thornicroft, a professor at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience, King’s College London, UK, and director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Research and Training in Mental Health, specializes in stigma, community psychiatry, global mental health, and guideline development in the European region. 17. The WHO Steering Group adhered to the WHO Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics (CRE) policy during the guideline development process. Prospective members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), External Review Group (ERG), and evidence teams were required to complete the WHO Declaration of Interests (DOI) form and submit their curriculum vitae for review to identify potential conflicts of interest. 18. The Wellcome Trust, an independent global charitable foundation focused on science and health, provided funding for the development of the guidelines. A representative of the funder attended the recommendations meeting as an observer, without participating in the decision-making process. 19. The External Review Group (ERG), composed of technical experts, employers, workers’ organizations, and individuals with lived experience of mental health, conducted a peer review of the draft guidelines. They provided technical feedback, identified factual errors, commented on language clarity, and addressed implementation, adaptation, and contextual issues. 20. Technical advisors from the International Labour Organization (ILO), led by Manal Azzi, provided expertise on occupational safety and health. The ILO, a tripartite United Nations agency, engaged key stakeholders, including the International Trade Union Confederation and the International Organisation of Employers, in the guideline development process.
